summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a Go binary that opens a remote-controlled PTY over WebRTC
details: The package's only payload is bin/sxt, a Linux/arm64 Go binary linking the pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, ice, turn, stun, dtls, srtp, sctp, mdns), coder/websocket, os/exec, and pty. Strings in the binary include the hardcoded signaling relay wss://relay.sextant.top and TURN endpoints. The combination establishes a peer-to-peer channel via that author-controlled signaling relay and pipes received bytes into a local pseudo-terminal, giving any peer that reaches the relay interactive shell access on the host running the binary. package.json declares no scripts, no main, and no bin; the tarball's sole purpose is delivering this binary. The license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, an author-controlled repository whose name and handle reinforce the remote-control intent of the shipped payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
